title: Beyond discounts: What will drive the next phase of India’s online grocery growth?
summary: The scale of this shift is evident in the numbers. Data from Bain & Company and Flipkart’s e-retail report underscores this reality, revealing that quick commerce accounted for more than two-thirds of India’s e-grocery orders in 2024, with the market scaling to an estimated $6–7 billion. This signals a fundamental change in shopping behaviour. Yet, for brands operating at the intersection of traditional food manufacturing and digital retail, the next growth opportunity lies in improving the fundamentals behind every transaction.
